budget_items.topic: Trust fund cy pres money for underserved residents
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the select board has refused to authorize the cy pres filings needed to release this money, split mainly between the American Legion Poor Fund, Post 283 Fund and the Worthy Poor Fund, to veterans and poor residents.

budget_items.topic: Susan Howard Fund missing money (1905 gift)
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said money Susan Howard gave to the town in 1905 no longer appears in the ledger and the town cannot locate it, and he wants it investigated.

budget_items.topic: Proposed override's tax impact on residents
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair argued the proposed override would raise typical tax bills by roughly this much a month, which he said makes trust fund assistance more necessary for seniors on fixed incomes.

budget_items.topic: Historical trailer-park water/sewer spending (context, not current budget)
figures_as_heard: million and a half$2 million dollars
budget_items.what_was_said: Richard recalled a roughly 20-year-old town decision to spend far more than a trailer park's assessed value on water and sewer service there, offering it as precedent for valuing people over a pure cost comparison.

budget_items.topic: Town's legal fees responding to the commission's breach notice
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair estimated the town is spending several thousand dollars on its attorney to answer the commission's 55-page filing rather than releasing the funds.

budget_items.topic: Cost of legal response versus cost of requested investigation
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the commission does not need to ask town meeting for this amount, but that the town may spend as much fighting the commission legally as it would cost to fund the requested investigations.

budget_items.topic: Nathaniel Day 1901 Worthy Poor Fund cy pres petition
budget_items.what_was_said: Town counsel's letter states this is the only fund currently requiring action and that a cy pres petition has been drafted for the commission's review and vote.

budget_items.topic: Hypothetical funding for fund investigations from the assistant town manager position
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said he would take this amount from money requested for a new assistant town manager position to pay for investigating the trust funds instead.
The chair said at this salary level the town manager should not need an assistant and should handle more of the workload herself.

Counsel's letter argues the fund is not obsolete because Lunenburg veterans eligible for Legion membership can still receive funds; the chair called this unworkable given the veterans agent's limited authority.
Counsel's letter states this fund has no found devise and is not eligible for administrative cy pres, and would require costly judicial action instead.

budget_items.topic: Potential litigation/expert costs for American Legion Poor Fund
budget_items.what_was_said: Counsel's letter cites the Woodward School for Girls case to say expert testimony for judicial cy pres litigation could cost this much over the life of a case.

budget_items.topic: J&M Howard sidewalk and grounds fund
budget_items.what_was_said: Counsel's letter cites a 1931 town meeting record showing a devise for this fund and says cy pres is not currently required; the chair said no formal devise document has actually been provided to the commission.
Counsel's letter says the fund's purpose is not obsolete because a gazebo exists on town land, so cy pres is not required; the chair asked why a formal devise has still not been drafted.
Counsel's letter says any 1972 recordkeeping questions are now moot under the statute of limitations and that the town holds no funds under this name requiring action.

decisions.decision: The chair will personally call town counsel to request the cy pres petition document for the Nathaniel Day Worthy Poor Fund before the commission votes on it.
A draft compliance/investigation-request letter concerning the school department's non-response on scholarship and trust records will be reviewed at the next meeting.

minutes.summary: The Trust Fund Commission chair used the meeting's public-comment period and most of the meeting itself to accuse the town manager and select board of stonewalling release of trust-fund money meant for veterans and the poor, and to read and rebut point-by-point a town counsel letter responding to the commission's breach notice on several trust funds (Nathaniel Day Worthy Poor Fund, American Legion Post 283 and Poor Funds, J&M Howard sidewalk fund, gazebo fund, Susan Howard fund). No cy pres filings were approved at this meeting; the commission agreed to request the drafted Nathaniel Day petition from counsel and to take up the school department's non-response to records requests at its next meeting, and it approved its prior meeting minutes before adjourning.

what_happened.line: The commission chair accused the town manager and select board of blocking release of trust-fund money meant for veterans and the poor.
No cy pres filings were approved; the commission will ask town counsel for the drafted Nathaniel Day petition before voting on it.
The chair read and disputed town counsel's letter fund by fund, covering the Legion funds, a sidewalk fund, a gazebo fund and the Susan Howard fund.
The commission flagged the school department's non-response to records requests on scholarship trust funds for its next meeting.
The commission approved its prior minutes and set its next meeting for May 21.

why_it_matters: Several town trust funds meant to help veterans and low-income residents remain unreleased while the commission and town counsel dispute which funds legally require a court or administrative filing to unlock.
The dispute also touches scholarship trust records held by the school department, which the commission says have gone unanswered.
Legal costs tied to this disagreement are being paid by the town while the underlying assistance money sits unspent.
